Ly.bar_b_note: Only the Old Bram frame stages a visible speaker; the Warder Solene frame shows the player alone on a flat yellow courtyard and the Keeper Hald frame is blocked by a brown slab of near-camera geometry, so the dialogue staging sinks it.

El.bar_b_note: Warm grass light and long shadows carry the meadow, but the defeated grunt stands in the same neutral pose in -01 and -99-after, and a creature sits half inside the hillside top-right in -00-before, so the defeat beat does not read.

Ap.bar_b_note: Side A's furred boar is close to the naturalistic bar but has odd yellow blotches and floats above its shadow in faint mid; side B is a smooth clay or plastic pig with pasted green moss, which reads as a toy. Neither stands clearly taller than the 1.80 m ruler.

Pe.bar_b_note: The fainted Terrapup is a small, pale, low-contrast lump that is the same in the fainted and resting frames, and the fainted Veridian is lost in the bushes, so the subject does not read even though the sky and the lakeside cottage give the backdrop some life.

Rx.bar_b_note: The navy panel with a teal frame and gold section heads is on palette, but small grey body text, literal '[Q] Previous tab / [Tab] Next tab' labels and a clipped 'Fighting' row under quick bindings keep it below a shipping menu.

Gy.bar_b_note: The furred Terrapup and Mudsnout read well in grass light, but in all three frames the ally overlaps the dark player silhouette and the opposing trainer is a small figure squeezed between the two creatures, so the fight camera sinks it.

Mg.bar_b_note: The standing Stormcapra matches the owner bar in fleece, horns and scale, and side A's tumble and side-down faint stay readable; side B's hit react reads, but its faint mid and faint end melt into a headless fleece blob with the horns stretched into tubes.

Xc.bar_b_note: The silver-haired villager has expressive eyes, a clear silhouette and an earthy green and brown outfit that fits the settlement palette; only the softer, more cartoon face than the naturalistic creatures holds it back.

Ue.bar_b_note: Side A gives each site its own aftermath: a banner torn down, a prisoner freed beside an open cage, a rune stone uncovered, a tent struck with smoke rising, and a banner on the ground. Side B leaves the enemy banners hanging at sites 1, 3 and 5 and simply deletes the cage at site 2. Both sides share smeared low-resolution ground at sites 2 and 4.

Yr.bar_b_note: The sky and the cloud layer are attractive, but a stiff trainer hangs like a peg under a Galecrest whose wingspan is barely wider than the trainer, over a blurred green ground plane with no midground.

Mq.bar_b_note: The torch-lit hall has warm mood, but turquoise guide rails cut across the floor and creatures, the Terrapup is blown out to a glowing orange, and frame -03 is blocked by a pillar in front of the camera.

top_changes.change: Fix combat and dialogue camera framing: keep the speaking trainer or opponent in frame, pull the camera back or offset it so the ally does not cover the player, and add collision so pillars and wall slabs (Ly Keeper Hald, Mq -03) never block the lens.

Author grounded defeat, faint and carry poses: defeated trainers kneel or slump, fainted creatures settle on their sides with distinct rest poses, the Fly carrier holds the trainer by the shoulders with the body angled, and faint end keeps the head and horns intact.

Replace the turquoise arena rails with a diegetic boundary (stone kerb, rune inlay or low light), remove the enemy banners in after frames, and raise the contrast and size of HUD body text while swapping literal key labels for controller glyphs.
